clue.text: Classical maiden tripping over down with unknown speed

indicators.note: tripping suggests stumbling about, so the letters of over and down are jumbled

parts.note: O is the cricket scoring abbreviation for an over
taken as written
Y is one of the algebraic unknowns
MPH, miles per hour, is a measure of speed

explanation.surface: A nymph of ancient myth stumbles across the downs at an unknown speed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' looks like part of 'tripping over', but it is the cricket O, joining the letters of 'down' in the jumble.
explanation.definitionFit: A wood nymph, or dryad, is a female spirit of Greek and Roman mythology.

clue.text: Demolition site where we play gets reported

parts.note: WE plus REC, the recreation ground or site for play, said together

explanation.surface: A demolition site where a children's playground used to be is in the news.
explanation.walkthrough: A rec, short for recreation ground, is a British public playing field; 'we' plus 'rec' sound like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A wreck is the destruction or ruin of something, as a demolition is.

clue.text: Stone chucked by a canoeist hit islands in the Pacific

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for the stone, a British unit of weight

explanation.surface: Someone paddling a canoe is struck by a thrown stone near Pacific islands.
explanation.walkthrough: Take ST out of A CANOEIST to leave A, C, A, N, O, E, I, which 'hit' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Oceania is the name for the region of Pacific islands including Polynesia, Melanesia and Micronesia.

clue.text: Obsessive leading lady departs in state

parts.note: NY is the abbreviation for the US state of New York
ER, Elizabeth Regina, the queen as the nation's leading lady

explanation.walkthrough: 'state' looks like a mood but is New York; ER is the Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: Nerdy describes someone obsessively absorbed in a specialised or technical interest.

clue.text: Anguished king's US subject accepting award

CBE, Commander of the Order of the British Empire, is a British honour

explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's Scottish king is tormented by guilt after murdering Duncan.

clue.text: Drone blocked by extension on current instrument

indicators.note: the drone word is blocked, or filled, by the other pieces placed in its middle

an arm is an extension, as of a building or organisation

explanation.definitionFit: A harmonium is a small reed organ played with pedal-pumped bellows.

clue.text: Broadcast overlooked film

explanation.walkthrough: 'film' looks like a movie but is a thin hazy layer.
explanation.definitionFit: A mist is a fine film of droplets, as on a window or lens.

clue.text: Little bit of poetry mother's penning

ODIC means relating to odes, so of poetry

explanation.walkthrough: 'penning' reads as writing but means enclosing.
explanation.definitionFit: A modicum is a small quantity of something.

clue.text: Subsidised do with no press involved

indicators.note: involved means tangled up, so these letters are mixed together

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.definitionFit: Something sponsored is funded or backed financially by a business or patron.

clue.text: Rapid measuring system Zeno introduced, oddly abandoned

indicators.note: introduced means brought in, so the letters go inside the other word

parts.note: the metric system is a system of measurement

explanation.surface: Zeno of Elea presented a quick system of measures, then strangely gave it up.
explanation.walkthrough: Zeno was a Greek philosopher famous for paradoxes of motion, which fits 'Rapid'.

clue.text: Spooner's US agent stuns night-time prowler

clue.text: Eatery within media company short of meat

parts.note: Sky is a British broadcasting and media company
an inn is a pub that serves food

explanation.surface: A restaurant inside a broadcaster's offices has run out of meat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'meat' reads as food on the menu but here means flesh on the body.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone skinny is thin, lacking flesh on their bones.

clue.text: Expert wished good riddance?

parts.note: a specialist who bids an evil spirit be gone from someone possessed

explanation.walkthrough: 'good riddance' is usually said with relief, but here the expert's whole job is getting rid of a demon.
explanation.definitionFit: An exorcist is a person who drives evil spirits out of the possessed.

clue.text: Member behind review of spots to stay under canvas

re-view read as viewing again, from the other end, so the spots word is turned around

parts.note: acne is a skin condition of spots
MP, Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A politician looks back over the spots chosen for a camping trip.
explanation.definitionFit: To encamp is to set up and live in a camp, sleeping in tents.

clue.text: Smuttier note increasingly snooty beginner dropped

parts.note: haughtier means more snooty

clue.text: Leading setter's charges immediately reduced

reduced means cut short, so the last letter goes

explanation.definitionFit: Prominent means leading or important, standing out from others.

parts.note: hairy is informal for risky or dodgy
MA, Master of Arts, a graduate degree

explanation.walkthrough: 'dodgy' looks like an anagram signal but is HAIRY; Ave Maria is the Latin prayer.
explanation.definitionFit: Hail Mary is the English version of the Ave Maria, the Catholic devotion to the Virgin.

clue.text: Glittering range of surplus trousers

indicators.note: a range of letters running across the two words holds the answer

explanation.surface: A sparkling selection of leftover trousers on sale.
explanation.definitionFit: Lustrous means shining, with a gleaming sheen.

clue.text: Infant clothing at hand after sunset?

indicators.note: clothing means wrapping around, so the infant word goes round the other

parts.note: a tot is a small child
nigh means near or at hand

explanation.definitionFit: Tonight is the evening of today, the hours once darkness falls.

clue.text: Team attending pub strip in window

a bar is a pub

clue.text: I'm surprised to receive back payment for strain

indicators.note: receive means take in, so the turned payment word goes inside

indicators.note: back means turned the other way round

parts.note: the dole is British state unemployment benefit

explanation.walkthrough: 'strain' looks like stress but is a tune.
explanation.definitionFit: A strain is a passage of music or tune, as is a melody.

clue.text: Tenancies cancelled, excuses being made

parts.note: lets are rental agreements, so tenancies
an event that is off has been cancelled

explanation.definitionFit: To let someone off is to excuse them from a duty or punishment.

clue.text: Pooh, investing first of his old pennies, made a nicker

indicators.note: investing means clothing or surrounding, so the bear's name goes around the letter

indicators.note: first of takes the first letter of his

parts.note: D was the abbreviation for pennies in pre-decimal British money

explanation.walkthrough: 'nicker' looks like a thief (nick is British slang for steal) but means a neigh.

clue.text: Revolutionary role as local ruler

parts.note: a part is a role in a play
taken as written

explanation.surface: A rebel's role as a regional governor.

clue.text: Weight plummeting in pig's fibrous tissue

parts.note: a swine is a pig; the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: A pig's sinews show the weight dropping away.

clue.text: Turn away 50% of travellers in distress

half the word, its first five letters

clue.text: Kid runs into club

parts.note: a bat is a club
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.walkthrough: 'club' looks like a nightclub but is a bat.
explanation.definitionFit: A brat is a badly behaved child.
